The policy framework for ADHD treatment quality in this corpus is structured around specific clinical indicators and guidelines overseen by the [[styregruppen|Styregruppen]]. The committee plays a central role in evaluating treatment quality, particularly emphasizing that non-pharmacological interventions remain vital for high-quality ADHD care [^src2]. To support this mandate, the [[styregruppen|Styregruppen]] utilizes the [[dmpg-retningslinje|DMPG-retningslinje]] for non-pharmacological treatment in its ongoing policy work with [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src2].

Policy implementation and performance targets are actively managed across the various indicators. A revised version of [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] has undergone consultation and is expected to be implemented within the coming months [^src1]. Furthermore, the framework establishes strict quantitative development targets (*udviklingsmål*) to measure clinical success. [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] has a development target of ≥ 90% [^src3]. Similarly, [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] has a development target of ≥ 90% specifically applying to the period from April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025 [^src4]. In contrast, there is currently no development target established for [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] [^src5].

  Type: policy

  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2024.pdf, pages 31-35

  Type: policy
